title: Profile rule catalog
description: Catalog of the profile rules: one source for hub (resolver, validation, migration), admin UI (editor, texts) and apps (labels, reason sentences). Semantics: docs/profiles.md. tools/validate.py checks the catalog against schemas/common/profile-rule-values.json and $defs/profile_rule_key, and every resolver vector in fixtures/profiles/resolve against the reference resolver tools/profiles_ref.py.

help.description: One sentence under the label. {brand} = display name from brand.json.

type.description: Shape of the value; the exact schema is schemas/common/profile-rule-values.json#/properties/<key>.

default.description: Catalog default (value of a new empty profile, and of a rule a profile does not contain yet after an update).

default_fixed.description: Checkbox “Fixed” of a new empty profile.

fixed_checkbox.description: false = the rule is always fixed (profile only, never adjusted per device).

user_choice_allowed.description: The value “User's choice” is possible (comfort rules only): the person at the device decides, the profile value is the starting value.

platforms.description: Platforms the rule applies to; elsewhere it resolves to not_applicable.

pro.description: The app offers this rule only with Pro; the hub shows a hint and does not check it. For a kids rule it means: the app on the child's device works only with Pro and without Pro controls nothing. It never means that a rule is dropped without Pro.

requires_child_protection.description: Kids rule: applies only to a profile with parental controls (else not_applicable / requires_child_protection).

profile_kinds.description: Kinds of profile the rule applies to; on a profile of another kind it resolves to not_applicable / requires_profile_kind. null = every kind.

order.description: Values from “less allowed” to “more allowed” (booleans and enums). Boundaries cap along this order; the admin UI uses it to detect a loosening.

strictest.description: Value of the rule for an expired guest (access_expired); null = unchanged (comfort and kids rules).

cap.description: Highest allowed value (along order). When cap is the first value of order, or the rule has no order, the boundary always decides the rule.

lifted_by.description: Optional: the boundary does not apply while this boolean rule resolves to true (parental controls: the rule watch only when the kids rule kids_watch allows it; hub_only: quick_access and watch only with remote_access). Absent = the boundary always applies.

boundaries.description: Boundaries that cap the rule. With order: capped along order. Without order (object rules, e.g. setup_devices): an active boundary always decides, the value is cap. A boundary with lifted_by does not apply while that rule resolves to true.

loosening_warning.description: Confirmation text when an admin loosens this rule (profile or device).

replaces.description: Former keys, columns or settings this rule replaces (documentation).

enforcement.description: Who enforces the rule: ha = Home Assistant (shown “Enforced”), hub = the hub (“Enforced”), app = the app only (“Applies in <brand>”).

enforcement_with_hub_path.description: Enforcement on a device whose effective rule control_path is hub (no Home Assistant key at home; it reads and switches through the hub, which checks the rule), with or without parental controls; null = the value of the checked path (enforcement_with_checked_path, since the device user is read-only in Home Assistant on the hub path too), else enforcement.

enforcement_with_checked_path.description: Enforcement on a device whose effective rule control_path is checked or hub (device user read-only in Home Assistant, switching through the integration action); null = same as enforcement. On the hub path enforcement_with_hub_path wins.

watch_limit.description: How a watch is limited to its phone in this rule (docs/protocol.md “Every watch follows its phone”): the limited value is the meet of both, never a replacement. none = not limited (comfort, display, kids and location rules); ordered = the stricter along order; areas = common area ids and common tags only (all = the other side; empty = no areas); schedule = only the minutes both access hours are open (off = always open; same hub time zone, overnight windows); remote_levels = the lower level for the default and every key either side names (a key of one side compared with the other's resolved level); kinds = enabled only when both are, common kinds only. Every rule must be classified (tools/profile_rules.py).

profile_kinds.description: The profile kinds ($defs/profile_kind) in display order, with labels, an icon and the platforms a device of this kind can have when it is set up (onboard_info.grant offers only kinds that fit the waiting device). guest_access = devices of this kind are set up as guest access with an expiry (guest, house sitter, babysitter). Watches have no kind of their own: a phone sets up its own watch with the watch's default profile.

source.description: Source that goes with this reason; null = profile or device.

admin.description: Sentence in the admin UI. Placeholders: {brand} (display name from brand.json), {profile}, {admin}, {value}, {profile_value}, {until}, {then}, {platform}.

device.description: Sentence on the device; null = not shown on the device.

rule.description: How the hub computes expires_at (hub time zone). Vectors: fixtures/profiles/expiry.

enforcement.description: Labels of the enforcement kinds for admin UI and apps (honest display).

expiry_limits.description: A temporary device adjustment ends at least min_minutes and at most max_days in the future (else 422 override.expires_at).

notifications.description: Priority thresholds (notification priority 0-100) of the rule notification_level: important from important_min_priority, critical from critical_min_priority (never suppressed).

safety_entities.description: Safety entities: notifications about them are never suppressed; with parental controls they are always visible read-only (controlling the alarm stays blocked); “When away” is at least view for them. No delivery promise: no push, the app shows them while open; the product is no alarm system.

max_hours.description: Hub maximum per grant (authoritative; the apps follow access.expires_at and have no own cap). Extending starts a new grant.
